evidence: Authored for this product: instruction.md:1 names HireOps and frames a recruiting team's two linked surfaces (pipeline board + per-application candidate conversations) with the multi-user 'nobody's work gets trampled' theme; hireops_rules.md sections 1-9 define HireOps-specific roles (Recruiter/Hiring manager/Observer/Candidate), six stages with Rejected-from memory and reopen-only-to-origin (lines 42-53), hand-set shared intra-stage order (55-59), Interview places 1-50 (28, 61-65), stale-version 409 with 'by whom' (75-80), board-order bulk move (87-92), undo semantics (94-100), 15 s live updates preserving typing/focus/open card/scroll (115-123), 30-message paging with scroll anchoring (142-147), per-person unread/seen (149-166), per-user per-browser drafts across sign-out (168-175), and a candidate-wording status table plus redaction list (177-194). task.toml: arena_slice='recruiting-hiring-operations', keywords recruiting/pipeline/messaging/realtime, provenance 'Adapted from the supplied HireOps task ... with an authored reference implementation and browser rubric', difficulty_explanation matches the brief. All template CHANGE_ME fields are replaced. app_context.md lists only HireOps accounts/screens; criterion ids are all hro_* (hro_job_open ... hro_drafts); seed has 10 users, 3 jobs (Platform Engineer, Data Analyst, Product Designer), 16 applications, 127 messages incl. a 120-message thread; grep of the whole frozen task for sibling names (pellmoor, threadline, torquebay, docketlight, bazaar, boardloom, colderwater, ridgeline, gridforge, patchpad, coursemark) and Pellmoor nouns (vacanc, panel member, funnel) returned nothing. Sibling comparison: the closest sibling by domain is projects/pellmoor-job-pipeline (also recruiting). Shared concepts exist: no stage skipping (hiring-rules.md line 3-4 vs hireops_rules.md 47-48), same person may apply to different jobs but not twice to one (hiring-rules.md 'must not appear twice against one vacancy' vs hireops_rules.md 32-33), a capacity cap (Pellmoor openings reserved by offers vs HireOps Interview places), atomic batch moves, and stale-version refusal. These are generic recruiting/concurrency mechanics, not a renamed copy: Pellmoor's core flows are interview panels with 1-5 scores, versioned assessment freshness, offer gating, opening reservation/fill conversion, idempotent receipts and a d3 funnel from stage history (criteria e.g. exact_derived_funnel, panel_change_invalidates_entire_assessment, receipt_identity_is_person_scoped...); none of those appear in HireOps. HireOps' core flows - recruiter-candidate messaging with paging/scroll anchoring, unread/seen, per-user drafts surviving session end, candidate-facing portal with wording table and redaction, hand-ordered shared stage order, single-step undo with conflict rules, and non-disruptive live updates - have no Pellmoor counterpart. Criteria sets differ in ids and observables. Threadline (team chat) overlaps on messaging mechanics (unread, load older without losing position) but is a channel/thread/reaction/webhook chat product, not a recruiting workspace; HireOps conversations are one-per-application with candidate/staff role asymmetry and 'seen' semantics. Counterexample attempts: (a) a grader/client comparing HireOps and Pellmoor as nouns-swapped: fails because more than half the HireOps brief (conversations, candidate portal, live non-disruption, undo, ordering) has no Pellmoor analogue and Pellmoor's panels/assessments/funnel/receipts are absent here. (b) a template-residue clone: no CHANGE_ME or other product name remains in brief, notes, context, prompts or metadata. Residual note (not a defect, no measurement required): no standalone suite domain-plan document was found in the workspace; fit to the plan is evidenced by the assigned slug/arena_slice 'recruiting-hiring-operations' and the provenance line. The suite does contain a second recruiting task (Pellmoor); if the client's plan requires one task per domain slice that is a portfolio decision outside this task's source, and the mechanics overlap listed above is the honest extent of similarity.
